kai: Heads-up — after the kernel-selector change on main (commit ab12c) we're seeing an 8–12% throughput drop on 8xA100 runs for medium-length sequences (~1–2k).

lena: seen it. Perf dashboard highlights a spike in all-reduce time during forward KV-sync. Not present on older run.

devon: suspect LL128 path is mis-selected for these collectives. Quick nvprof shows allreduce ~11.9ms vs expected ~4ms on the same mesh.

maria: can you paste the profiler snippet you saw?

kai: pasted below (trimmed):
```
# nvprof summary (trimmed)
all_reduce         11.9ms   (nvlink)
kernel_selector     0.8ms
compute             3.6ms
other comms         0.3ms
```
Also we see `NCCL_ALGO=auto` and `NCCL_PROTO=unspecified` in the job env.

lena: try forcing `NCCL_PROTO=LL` on a repro job — I suspect a fallback to proto/LL128 because of chunking heuristics for small messages.

devon: did an A/B yesterday: forcing LL128 reduced allreduce to ~4.1ms but introduced head-of-line stalls in channels for some configs. Forcing proto gives stable but slower (≈12ms). So it's a tradeoff.

maria: another angle — channel count. Our allocator currently uses `min(cards*2, 16)` which can oversubscribe channels for medium seq lengths and cause contention. If collectives are small, fewer channels with larger chunks might win.

kai: proposal: add a conservative "channel_fade" heuristic that decays number of channels when KV-cache hit_rate > 0.9 AND median_seq_len < 2048. Also make kernel-selector incorporate an estimated allreduce cost model (approx based on bytes_per_collective and channel_count).

devon: plan to run 4 short experiments tonight:
  1) force `NCCL_PROTO=LL128`
  2) clamp channels to 4 (override allocator)
  3) enable `channel_fade` with decay=0.5
  4) proto + larger chunk_size (increase chunk by 2x)
I'll post micro-benchmarks and end-to-end throughput.

infra-bot: perf job queued — https://perf.redwood/test/3421 (status: queued) :hourglass_flowing_sand: 

lena: also log `kvcache.hit_rate` and `kvcache.prefetch_bytes` into the perf trace so we can correlate. Last time that telemetry helped find a bad prefetch size.

kai: good call. If experiments show wins, we land a conservative heuristic with telemetry and a quick regen test to catch future regressions. Keep changes behind a feature flag to rollback fast.

devon: quick update after the first two runs (smoke):
  - clamp channels=4 => +6% avg throughput, variance low
  - channel_fade (decay=0.5) => +7% avg, slightly better p95
  - force LL128 => +12% but p99 increases a lot (variance)
  - proto + bigger chunk => improved steady-state but still slower than LL128 baseline
I'll upload the perf traces and annotated flame graphs after the full run.

maria: excellent — sounds like the real fix is a smarter selector that considers kvcache hit-rate, seq_len distribution, and channel contention. We can gate on telemetry to tune thresholds.

kai: thanks all. Action items: (1) devon post full traces, (2) lena add kvcache metrics to trace, (3) maria prototype channel_fade config, (4) I'll draft selector-change RFC and rollback plan.

devon: putting results and traces into the perf ticket once the long runs finish. Will ping here when ready. :thumbsup:
